## Setup
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidytext)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(quanteda)
library(quanteda.textstats)
library(knitr)
library(udpipe)
```

## Approach 1
```{r}
# Data Loading
text_files <- list.files(
  path = "texts",
  pattern = "\\.txt$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

length(text_files)

texts_df <- tibble(
  file_path = text_files,
  document = tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(text_files)),
  text_original = map_chr(text_files, read_file)
)

texts_df %>%
  select(document) %>%
  kable(caption = "Documents in the corpus")
```
```{r}
# Remove Long S
texts_df <- texts_df %>%
  mutate(
    text_norm = str_replace_all(text_original, "ſ", "s"),
    text_norm = str_to_lower(text_norm),
    text_norm = str_replace_all(text_norm, "\\s+", " ")
  )

normalization_check <- texts_df %>%
  summarise(
    long_s_before = sum(str_count(text_original, "ſ")),
    long_s_after = sum(str_count(text_norm, "ſ"))
  )

normalization_check
```
```{r}
# DFM Construction
corp <- corpus(
  texts_df$text_norm,
  docnames = texts_df$document
)

toks <- tokens(
  corp,
  remove_punct = TRUE,
  remove_numbers = TRUE,
  remove_symbols = TRUE
)

# Stop words Removal
custom_stop <- c(
  "vnto", "haue", "doo", "hath", "bee", "ye", "thee", "hee",
  "shall", "hast", "doe", "beene", "thereof", "thus",
  "unto", "have", "doth", "upon"
)

toks <- tokens_remove(
  toks,
  pattern = c(stopwords("en"), custom_stop)
)

dfm_mat <- dfm(toks)

dfm_mat
topfeatures(dfm_mat, 25)
```
```{r}
# Compute TF-IDF weights and convert them to matrix
dfm_tfidf_mat <- dfm_tfidf(dfm_mat)
tfidf_matrix <- as.matrix(dfm_tfidf_mat)

# Extract top 15 TF-IDF terms for each document
top_tfidf_terms <- map_dfr(
  rownames(tfidf_matrix),
  function(doc) {
    scores <- tfidf_matrix[doc, ]

    tibble(
      document = doc,
      term = names(sort(scores, decreasing = TRUE))[1:15],
      tfidf = sort(scores, decreasing = TRUE)[1:15]
    )
  }
)

top_tfidf_terms %>%
  mutate(tfidf = round(tfidf, 3)) %>%
  kable(
    caption = "Top 15 TF-IDF Terms by Document",
    col.names = c("Document", "Term", "TF-IDF")
  )
```

## Approach 2
```{r}
# Remove very rare terms
dfm_cor <- dfm_trim(dfm_mat, min_termfreq = 5)

# Compute pairwise Pearson correlations between documents
sim_r <- textstat_simil(
  dfm_cor,
  margin = "documents",
  method = "correlation"
)

r_mat <- as.matrix(sim_r)
```


```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=6}
r_mat <- round(r_mat, 3)
# Long format for ggplot
heat_df <- as.data.frame(r_mat) %>%
  rownames_to_column("doc_i") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -doc_i,
    names_to = "doc_j",
    values_to = "r"
  )

# Keep documents in matrix order, with the diagonal running from the upper-left corner to the lower-right corner
doc_order <- rownames(r_mat)

heat_df <- heat_df %>%
  mutate(
    doc_i = factor(doc_i, levels = rev(doc_order)),
    doc_j = factor(doc_j, levels = doc_order)
  )

# Shorten long document names for display
short_labels <- function(x) {
  str_remove(x, "__.*$")
}

# Create the similarity heatmap
ggplot(heat_df, aes(x = doc_j, y = doc_i, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile() +
  coord_fixed() +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = short_labels) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = short_labels) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "blue",
    mid = "white",
    high = "red",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-1, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Pearson Correlation Between Documents",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Pearson r"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r}
# Extract each unique document pair
pair_index <- which(upper.tri(r_mat), arr.ind = TRUE)

pair_results <- tibble(
  document_1 = rownames(r_mat)[pair_index[, 1]],
  document_2 = colnames(r_mat)[pair_index[, 2]],
  r = r_mat[pair_index]
)

# Two most similar pairs
pair_results %>%
  arrange(desc(r)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 2)

# Two least similar pairs
pair_results %>%
  arrange(r) %>%
  slice_head(n = 2)
```

## Approach 3

I selected A06791 and A93819 because they have the lowest Pearson correlation (r = 0.135) and different distinctive vocabulary.
This comparison explores whether their lexical differences are accompanied by differences in syntactic structure.

```{r}
# Select two documents
syntax_texts <- texts_df %>%
  filter(document %in% c("A06791", "A93819")) %>%
  mutate(
    # Normalize long s and whitespace while preserving capitalization
    text_syntax = text_original %>%
      str_replace_all("ſ", "s") %>%
      str_replace_all("\\s+", " ")
  )

dir.create("models", showWarnings = FALSE)

model_files <- list.files(
  "models",
  pattern = "english-ewt.*\\.udpipe$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

if (length(model_files) == 0) {
  model_info <- udpipe_download_model(
    language = "english-ewt",
    model_dir = "models"
  )
  model_file <- model_info$file_model
} else {
  model_file <- model_files[1]
}
```

```{r}
# Load the model and annotate only the selected texts
ud_model <- udpipe_load_model(model_file)

anno_df <- map2_dfr(
  syntax_texts$text_syntax,
  syntax_texts$document,
  function(txt, doc) {
    udpipe_annotate(
      ud_model,
      x = txt,
      doc_id = doc
    ) %>%
      as.data.frame()
  }
) %>%
  rename(document = doc_id)
```

```{r}
# Identify syntactic features
syntax_df <- anno_df %>%
mutate(
is_word = upos != "PUNCT", 


is_clause = (upos %in% c("VERB", "AUX")) &
            str_detect(coalesce(feats, ""), "VerbForm=Fin"),

# Dependent clause
is_dep_clause = dep_rel %in% c(
  "advcl", 
  "ccomp",
  "xcomp",
  "acl",
  "acl:relcl"
),

is_coord = dep_rel %in% c("conj", "cc"),

# Nominal complexity: these relations make noun phrases more complex
is_complex_nominal = dep_rel %in% c(
  "amod",
  "nmod",
  "compound", 
  "appos"
)

)

# Aggregate features by sentence
sentence_df <- syntax_df %>%
  filter(is_word) %>%
  group_by(document, paragraph_id, sentence_id) %>%
  summarise(
    sentence = first(sentence),
    words = n(),
    clauses = sum(is_clause, na.rm = TRUE),
    dep_clauses = sum(is_dep_clause),
    coordination = sum(is_coord),
    complex_nominals = sum(is_complex_nominal),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate document-level measures
syntax_summary <- sentence_df %>%
  group_by(document) %>%
  summarise(
    sentences = n(),
    total_words = sum(words),
    clauses = sum(clauses),
    dependent_clauses = sum(dep_clauses),
    coordination = sum(coordination),
    complex_nominals = sum(complex_nominals),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    MLS = total_words / sentences,
    C_per_S = clauses / sentences,
    DC_per_C = if_else(clauses > 0, dependent_clauses / clauses, NA_real_),
    DC_per_S = dependent_clauses / sentences,
    Coord_per_C = if_else(clauses > 0, coordination / clauses, NA_real_),
    Coord_per_S = coordination / sentences,
    CN_per_C = if_else(clauses > 0, complex_nominals / clauses, NA_real_),
    CN_per_S = complex_nominals / sentences
  )

# Combine all measures
all_measures <- syntax_summary %>%
  select(
    document, MLS, C_per_S, DC_per_C, DC_per_S,
    Coord_per_C, Coord_per_S, CN_per_C, CN_per_S
  )

# Display a clearly formatted HTML table
knitr::kable(
  all_measures,
  format = "html",
  digits = 2,
  align = c("l", rep("r", 8)),
  caption = "Syntactic Complexity Comparison",
  col.names = c(
    "Document", "MLS", "C/S", "DC/C", "DC/S",
    "Coord/C", "Coord/S", "CN/C", "CN/S"
  ),
  table.attr = 'style="width:100%; border-collapse:collapse;"'
)
```
```{r}
example_candidates <- sentence_df %>%
  group_by(document) %>%
  arrange(desc(dep_clauses), desc(words), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 3) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(
    document, sentence, words, clauses,
    dep_clauses, coordination, complex_nominals
  )

example_candidates %>%
  kable(caption = "Candidate Sentences for Close Reading")
```
